sources.entry: OpenInCode - Finder toolbar app to open current folder in Visual Studio Code.

summary.one_liner: A small native macOS utility that adds a Finder toolbar button to open the current folder (or the folder containing a selected item) in Visual Studio Code.
summary.what_it_does: Open in Code is a macOS app that places a button in the Finder toolbar. Clicking it opens a folder in Visual Studio Code without using a terminal. If a folder is selected in Finder, that folder opens. If a file or package is selected, its containing folder opens. If multiple items are selected, the first item's folder opens. If nothing is selected, the folder shown in the front Finder window opens. It prefers Visual Studio Code and falls back to Visual Studio Code Insiders. The README describes installation via Homebrew cask or a direct download from GitHub Releases, and explains how to add the button to the toolbar by Command-dragging it.
use_cases: open the current Finder folder in VS Code
launch a project in VS Code from Finder
open the folder containing a selected file in an editor
add a one-click editor button to the Finder toolbar
open VS Code Insiders from Finder
avoid navigating to a folder in Terminal before opening it in an editor
how_to_run: Or download Open in Code.app from GitHub Releases and move it to /Applications
Hold Command and drag Open in Code to the Finder toolbar
Click Open in Code in a Finder window to open the folder in VS Code
Grant Finder automation permission on first use (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Automation)
notable: Finder-aware: uses the current selection, or the front Finder window when nothing is selected
Falls back from Visual Studio Code to Visual Studio Code Insiders
Installable via a Homebrew cask or direct download
Build, test, and packaging details are kept in CONTRIBUTING.md
caveats: Requires Visual Studio Code or Visual Studio Code Insiders to be installed
Needs Finder automation permission granted by the user; if denied, it must be re-enabled in System Settings
